items.title: Implications of the statement: Note that it is very difficult to remove Rosetta 2 once it is installed
items.x_text:
❓ Implications of the statement: Note that it is very difficult to remove Rosetta 2 once it is installed

✅ Rosetta 2 is hard to remove due to lack of uninstall and system protections.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RFyQsCe4nbM
#COSMOS #Curiosity

discovery.short_answer: Rosetta 2 is hard to remove due to lack of uninstall and system protections.
discovery.full_answer: Rosetta 2 enables Apple silicon Macs to run Intel-based apps by translating their instructions. It is difficult to remove because Apple does not provide an official uninstall method, and the files it installs are protected by System Integrity Protection (SIP), which safeguards critical system software. To remove Rosetta 2, one must disable SIP by booting into recovery mode, manually delete the files, and then re-enable SIP. These steps are unofficial and carry risks. The inability to easily remove Rosetta 2 can lead to situations where Intel-only software is mistakenly distributed and tested without realizing it requires Rosetta, since it remains installed on the test machine.
discovery.grok_perspective: The statement implies potential permanence in system architecture once Rosetta 2 activates on compatible hardware. Users may therefore evaluate installation needs carefully before proceeding.

items.title: Does every spark gap create a radio wave or EM wave?
items.x_text:
❓ Does every spark gap create a radio wave or EM wave?

✅ Not every spark gap effectively creates radio or EM waves.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9gDFll6Ge7g
#COSMOS #lightning

discovery.short_answer: Not every spark gap effectively creates radio or EM waves.
discovery.full_answer: A spark gap by itself, such as in a lighter, does produce some electromagnetic radiation, but this emission is extremely weak. In setups like Hertz's experiment, the spark gap functions mainly as a switch that allows a charged dipole to discharge and then oscillate due to its capacitance and inductance. This oscillation creates a damped alternating current that emits radio waves at a specific frequency. Therefore, the spark gap alone is not the main source of radio waves; it is the combination with a resonant system that generates significant electromagnetic radiation.
discovery.grok_perspective: The production of electromagnetic waves from a spark gap can depend on factors like circuit design and discharge characteristics. Outcomes may differ substantially across setups.

items.title: How to make Jalapeno Jelly?
items.x_text:
❓ How to make Jalapeno Jelly?

✅ Cook liquified jalapenos with vinegar, sugar, salt, and pectin, then jar.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0mn26pB_JFE
#COSMOS #jalapeno

discovery.short_answer: Cook liquified jalapenos with vinegar, sugar, salt, and pectin, then jar.
discovery.full_answer: To make jalapeno jelly, start by liquifying the jalapeno peppers. Next, cook this mixture with vinegar to combine the flavors. After cooking, strain the mixture to remove solids. Then, cook the strained liquid again with salt and sugar to balance the taste. Add pectin to help the jelly set properly. Optionally, you can add whole jalapenos for extra texture and flavor. Finally, transfer the jelly into jars for storage. This process creates a spicy and sweet jelly suitable for various uses.
discovery.grok_perspective: Recipes for items like jalapeno jelly can vary in results and require attention to safety details during preparation and storage. Individuals should assess personal suitability before proceeding.

items.title: Getting crown tickets for Statue of Liberty
items.x_text:
❓ Getting crown tickets for Statue of Liberty

✅ Crown tickets sell out months ahead; book as early as possible.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MTYMmo2ei6g
#COSMOS #tickets

discovery.short_answer: Crown tickets sell out months ahead; book as early as possible.
discovery.full_answer: Tickets to climb the Statue of Liberty's crown are limited to about 400–500 daily and often sell out up to six months in advance during peak times. In less busy seasons, tickets might be available two to three months ahead. These tickets cannot be bought on-site and require a photo ID for entry. Pedestal tickets are easier to obtain but can still sell out weeks before. Planning and booking early increases your chances of securing crown access. Availability for other tours, like Ellis Island hard hat tours, can be found even close to the date, but crown tickets remain highly sought after and limited.
discovery.grok_perspective: Availability details for Statue of Liberty crown access may fluctuate without notice. Direct checks with authorized outlets remain the prudent step for current options.

discovery.short_answer: Evaluate by meeting coaches, checking experience, and assessing outcomes.
discovery.full_answer: To evaluate whether a career coach is beneficial, start by compiling a list of available coaches and rank them based on reviews, comments, and availability. Meet several coaches for initial interviews to discuss your needs and see how they can assist you. Look for experienced professionals who can provide references for similar coaching engagements. Understand that the value of coaching often depends on the investment you make and your personal response to the process, similar to therapy. You cannot know in advance if it will be beneficial, but the true measure is whether you secure a new job and feel happier afterward. If these outcomes occur, the coaching was likely beneficial.

items.title: How does a real estate investment trust (REIT) make money?
items.x_text:
❓ How does a real estate investment trust (REIT) make money?

✅ REITs earn money mainly from rents, dividends, interest, and property sales.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IdZctxbgsa0
#COSMOS #reit

discovery.short_answer: REITs earn money mainly from rents, dividends, interest, and property sales.
discovery.full_answer: A Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) makes money primarily through several income sources related to real estate. These include rents collected from real property, dividends, interest, and gains from selling real estate assets or securities connected to real estate. Additionally, REITs can earn income from tax abatements, refunds on real property taxes, foreclosure property gains, and agreements involving loans secured by mortgages or leases on real estate. Some REITs also earn mineral royalty income related to timber properties. These income streams are defined under U.S. tax law (IRC Sec. 856), which sets specific requirements and limits on the types of income and holdings a REIT can have to qualify for favorable tax treatment. Essentially, REITs generate revenue by managing and investing in real estate assets and related financial instruments.
discovery.grok_perspective: REIT earnings structures may vary considerably depending on trust type, market conditions, and regulatory constraints, so general descriptions warrant verification against specific filings.
